svg.text: THE FASTENER SANDWICH AT ONE MAGNET
True section through one magnet position, drawn at one scale on both axes - 4.6 px/mm across AND through. One drawing per distinct stack shape.
Plate 4.75 mm (0.187 in), hole O6.5 mm, stud a fixed 10.00 mm (0.394 in). Change any of those and every panel here changes with it.
The orange band is where that part actually touches the plate. M6 nut and washer heights are DIN nominal; McMaster part numbers are NOT VERIFIED (2026-09-02).
Washer thickness is the MAX of the range it is sold to - every stack is checked against the thickest one that might ship.
Showing the 7 stack shapes that fit or are marginal, out of 24 permutations. Threadlocker changes locking, not geometry, so it has no separate panel - see fastener_matrix.svg for all of them.
JAM nut, DIN 439 + FENDER washer M6 DIN 9021, O18
JAM nut, DIN 439 + flat washer M6 DIN 125, O12
THIN nylon-insert locknut, DIN 985 low + FENDER washer M6 DIN 9021, O18
THIN nylon-insert locknut, DIN 985 low + flat washer M6 DIN 125, O12
USE: THIN nylon-insert locknut, DIN 985 low
4.75 + 0.00 + 4.00 = 8.75 mm against a 10.00 mm stud: +1.25 mm to spare, 45 mm2 of bearing, locking mechanical.
The stud length is an ESTIMATE (10 mm from two vendors' 32 x 18 mm overall figure; K&J do not print it). A washer costs 1.6 mm here, which is why the specified stack has none.
Bearing is harmless at every one of these: the plate is 36 ksi steel. The choice is thread length and locking, nothing else.
Fasteners are BLACK OXIDE where stocked - only the ARM nuts are visible, facing up against a textured-black arm.
